name: Do coins fall into large token unlocks?

sections.hypothesis: Coins fall behind the other coins in the 30 days before a large scheduled token unlock. If so, an altcoin portfolio should not hold a coin into a large unlock (an exit rule, beside the delisting and perp-listing rules).
sections.rationale: Who pays: early investors and teams whose tokens unlock are sellers in waiting, and the date is public months ahead, so holders who expect the selling sell first (front-running), and buyers wait until after it. Outside evidence: token-unlock price pressure is widely reported by unlock trackers and exchanges' research (Keyrock, 'From Locked to Liquidity: What 16,000+ Token Unlocks Teach Us': about 90% of unlocks saw negative price pressure, starting about 30 days before the date, worst for team unlocks), and the equity analogue is well established: share prices fall into IPO lock-up expiries, which are also known in advance (Field and Hanka 2001, Journal of Finance, 'The Expiration of IPO Share Lockups'). Not a rejected family: a scheduled event, like the delisting and perp-listing studies, not a chart pattern. Suggested by two outside AI reviews (2026-11-16 and 2026-11-18). Disclosed: the schedules come from DefiLlama's public dataset files as documented today; a schedule revised after the fact could add or move an event that wasn't known 30 days ahead (a mild lookahead the study can't rule out). Runs: one, a raw-effect study.
sections.rules: Data: DefiLlama's public emission files (defillama-datasets.llama.fi/emissions/<protocol>, 376 protocols listed on 2026-11-18), ingested once, before any return is read. Each protocol maps to a Binance spot coin by its CoinGecko id's ticker (from CoinGecko's public coin list): <TICKER>USDT; a ticker that two protocols or two CoinGecko ids share is dropped, and the mapping is written to a file and recorded before any return is read. Events: each documented unlock day of a mapped coin, of the exploration half plus BTC, ETH and SOL (never the locked confirmation half), where the tokens unlocked that day (summed over every section of the schedule) are at least 2% of the cumulative unlocked supply the day before, between 2020-01-01 and the last day whose window ends before 2025-11-01; the coin must have 60 days of unbroken spot history before day -30. Unlocks within 30 days of a previous event of the same coin are merged into the first. Day 0 is the unlock day. Primary window: day -30's open to day 0's open (the month before the unlock, where Keyrock finds the pressure), abnormal = the coin's return minus the equal-weighted mean of every other coin of the universe over the same window (kestrel.studies.events, no window across a break in a coin's history). Reported, deciding nothing: day 0 to day 14 (a relief bounce), day -14 to day 0, the split by recipient (sections DefiLlama files as insiders, team or investors against the rest), the split by unlock size against the coin's 30-day median daily volume (above and below the median ratio), and by year. Events on the same day are averaged into one; the bootstrap runs over event days. Placebo: for each coin, 200 random days (seed 0) at least 60 days from any of its unlocks, the same window.
sections.falsification: EXIT RULE (worth a rule in the altcoin portfolio's note) only if all hold: at least 50 event days; the mean 30-day abnormal return before the unlock is at most -3%; its bootstrap P(< 0) is at least 90% (5,000 resamples, seed 0); and it is below at least 90% of the placebo means. INSUFFICIENT if fewer than 50 event days (the mapping may leave few coins). Otherwise KILL. Run once.
sections.parameters: Fixed before any return was read: 2% of cumulative unlocked supply, 30-day primary window ending at day 0's open, 30-day merge, 60 days of history, 200 placebo days a coin at least 60 days from any unlock, 5,000 resamples, seed 0. No other threshold or window is tried; a change is a new version with a reason.
sections.costs: A measurement, not a strategy run: returns before costs. The -3% bar is set against the cost of acting on it (selling a held coin and buying it back after: about 0.5% for a small coin). Not a trial (a raw-effect study), recorded in the findings.

history.reason: KILL by its pre-registered test (findings 19, 2026-11-21): +0.4% against the other coins in the 30 days before (P(< 0) 47%); the same coins on random days did worse (-4.5%). Rejected (Luke).
